extraFacts.fact: Wave 4 products are API certified and supplied with the API monogram by API-licensed manufacturers to the applicable specification: API 6A, API 16A, API 16C, API 16D or API 7K.
NACE MR0175 / ISO 15156 sets material requirements for equipment used in H2S-containing oil and gas production.

API 6A product specification level (PSL 1 to 4) sets the inspection, testing and traceability applied; PR1 and PR2 are the performance requirement levels, PR2 having passed API 6A design-validation testing. PSL 3G adds a gas test.

faqs.q: What is a 720 psi knock-out drum used for on a well-test flare line?
faqs.a: A knock-out drum separates liquid droplets carried by gas on the way to the flare stack, so liquid does not reach the flare. This unit is rated 720 psi MAWP, 60-inch OD by 12-ft, ASME U-stamped and built with NACE MR-0175 compliant materials.

faqs.q: What do 60-in OD × 12-ft and 720 psi mean on this knock-out drum?
faqs.a: 60-in OD × 12-ft is the vessel size, 60 inches outside diameter and 12 feet long, and 720 psi is the MAWP, the maximum allowable working pressure. Capacity and rating are customised per client demand.

faqs.q: How does a knock-out drum separate liquid from gas?
faqs.a: Separation is by gravity: the internal geometry slows the inlet flow so droplets fall out of the gas stream. The 60-inch by 12-ft drum has hi/lo level sensors and a liquid-level gauge so the liquid can be drained before it builds up.

faqs.q: Can the 720 psi knock-out drum be sized for a different capacity or rating?
faqs.a: Yes. Capacity and pressure rating are customised per client demand, so give the gas rate, liquid load and pressure on the RFQ. The 60-inch OD by 12-ft vessel at 720 psi is the listed configuration.

faqs.q: What is the pressure rating of the 720 psi knock-out drum?
faqs.a: The drum is rated 720 psi MAWP and ASME U-stamped, with a pressure safety valve (PSV) fitted to protect it. Operate below the MAWP with the margin your procedure requires, and keep the PSV set pressure within the vessel rating.

faqs.q: Is the 720 psi knock-out drum suitable for sour gas?
faqs.a: The drum is built with NACE MR-0175 compliant materials, per the listing, so it can be used where the flare gas carries H2S. Give the H2S content on the RFQ so the wetted materials are confirmed.

faqs.q: Which codes apply to the 720 psi knock-out drum?
faqs.a: The pressure vessel is ASME U-stamped and the materials are NACE MR-0175 compliant, as stated on the listing. Third-party inspection and data book requirements are agreed on the quotation.

faqs.q: What instruments and fittings come on the knock-out drum?
faqs.a: The drum has a PSV, hi/lo level sensors and a liquid-level gauge on the vessel. It sits between the well-test spread and the flare stack; see the [flare stack](/c/wt-flare-stack) shelf for the stack and the [well testing equipment guide](/blog/surface-well-testing-equipment).

faqs.q: How is the knock-out drum installed ahead of a flare stack?
faqs.a: Install it in the gas line to the flare, upstream of the stack, with the drain and liquid-level gauge accessible so liquid can be removed regularly. Keep the PSV discharge piped to a safe location.

faqs.q: Knock-out drum or surge tank on a well-test spread: what is the difference?
faqs.a: A knock-out drum removes liquid droplets from the gas going to the flare, while a surge tank collects and measures liquid. See the [surge tank](/c/wt-surge-tank) shelf for liquid handling.
